subject: SLO handoff: latency & cost levers for Streamly integration
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@streamly.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@streamly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Sep 2027 14:12:00 -0000
Subject: SLO handoff: latency & cost levers for Streamly integration

Alex/Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so your engineering team has a clean handoff from discovery. I attached a draft SLO worksheet (streamly-slo-draft.xlsx) and a short trace we captured from the test harness.

High-level points you confirmed on the call:
- Primary SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 300ms for 128-token outputs (interactive editor flows).
- Peak concurrent users in pilot: ~220 active editors (bursty, regional US peak).
- Streaming requirement: partial tokens must arrive within 80–120ms of initial token generation for UX feel.
- Cost target for pilot: unit inference spend ~0.02–0.04 USD per request (goal).

Initial technical tradeoffs we recommended:
1) Continuous batching: enable runtime continuous batching with max_batch_delay_ms=10–15ms to aggregate many small requests without violating tail latency. This saves GPU cycles and meets cost target.
2) Client-side prefix caching + server KV cache warmup: cache user prompt prefixes in Redis/KV to avoid reconstructing long context; warmup hot keys before peak windows to reduce cold-LRU misses.
3) Quantization profiles: evaluate q8_0 vs q4_0 for your main model path. q8_0 gives ~1.6x speed improvement with minimal quality drop; q4_0 can halve memory but needs per-prompt evals for hallucination risk.
4) Model variants and fallback: primary model = medium-sized streaming model; fallback to a faster small_variant for tail/backfill requests or nondestructive previews.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Rishi: can you run the attached trace through the runtime estimator and push back numeric estimates for p95 with/without continuous batching and with q8_0?
- Streamly: share a representative 1-hour production-ish trace (anonymized) and your current concurrency profile by minute.
- Marissa: I'll prepare a concise Ops runbook for warmup + autoscale windows and share a Drive folder (linked).

I think we should sync again early next week to review the numeric estimates and narrow the model path. If you prefer a live walkthrough of the estimator, we can schedule 30 minutes.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Subject: RE: SLO handoff: latency & cost levers for Streamly integration

Thanks — quick engineering notes after looking at the trace:

- Baseline: without batching and with fp16 on the medium model, p95 is ~420ms for 128 tokens (matches their test harness).
- Continuous batching (max_batch_delay_ms=12ms) reduces p95 to ~260–290ms depending on request size distribution; tail (p99) improves but we need warm caches for best results.
- KV/prefix cache: a small Redis-backed prefix cache with TTL 30m reduces average decode tokens by ~18% on this trace. That translates to ~12–15% cost savings.
- Quant profiles: q8_0 on the medium model reduces per-token latency by ~25% and memory by ~20%; q4_0 reduces memory further but increases CPU pre/post-processing overhead and a small quality delta — needs eval.

Open questions for Streamly before we finalize a recommended config:
1) How sensitive is your UX to rare generation glitches? If you can tolerate a few low-confidence completions, q4_0 becomes attractive for cost.
2) Are you planning dedicated capacity or shared hosted for pilot? Dedicated reduces p99 variance.

I'll produce a 1-page comparison table (fp16 vs q8_0 vs q4_0) and run the same trace through the estimator for the small_variant fallback path. Targeting to have that by tomorrow noon PT.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@streamly.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 06 Sep 2027 01:48:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SLO handoff: latency & cost levers for Streamly integration

Thanks for the rapid turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can tolerate a small number of lower-confidence completions but not visible truncation glitches in the editor. UX team prefers q8_0 as first pass, q4_0 only for background/async tasks.
- Pilot will likely use hosted capacity initially; we may convert to dedicated for GA if latency variance becomes an issue.
- We'll anonymize and upload an hour of production-ish traffic (5000 requests w/ burst patterns) to the Drive link you shared by EOD your time.

One cost constraint: our procurement team wants to see an estimate where unit inference cost stays <= $0.035 for 128-token interactive requests at 95% load. Can you include the unit cost projection for two model-paths: (A) medium fp16 + continuous batching + KV cache, (B) medium q8_0 + continuous batching + KV cache + small_variant fallback for 12% of requests.

Also, any immediate ops recommendations for warm start? We saw 30–45s cold KV misses in one of the traces which spiked p99.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Streamly

Subject: RE: SLO handoff: latency & cost levers for Streamly integration

Great — appreciate the detail. Quick action items and what we'll deliver this week: 

1) Rishi will send the fp16 / q8_0 / q4_0 comparison and numeric p95/p99 estimates for the attached trace by tomorrow noon PT (includes unit-cost projection for the two model-paths Alex requested).
2) Ops runbook: Marissa will draft a short warm-start playbook covering prefix pre-warming, KV TTLs (start 30m), and a suggested autoscale policy (scale-up threshold: 75% GPU util, cooldown 90s). She'll drop it into the Drive folder.
3) Streamly: upload anonymized 1-hour trace to Drive and paste the HubSpot deal link in the thread.
4) Follow-up: 30-minute sync Wed 09:00 PT to review numbers and lock the pilot config. I'll send a calendar invite.

Notes on warm-start / immediate mitigations for KV cold misses:
- Pre-warm strategy: run a lightweight warmup job that issues prioritized prefix lookups 10 minutes before known peak windows. This brings KV hit rate up from ~40% to ~85% for hot prefixes in our experience.
- Fallback policy: if KV misses exceed threshold or backend queue depth spikes, temporarily widen batching window (max_batch_delay_ms -> 25ms) and route low-priority requests to small_variant until caches warm.

I'll attach the calendar invite and the Drive folder link when Marissa populates the runbook. Thanks — feeling good about hitting the p95 target with the q8_0 path + continuous batching and prefix caching.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
